content.text:
Yes — optimized. **0.82 → 1.51 Mtok/s** at the training shape (+84%). Four changes:

1. **Shared sparse indexer.** Old: each of the 9 attention modules owned its own indexer, so every forward (with 4 loop iterations = ~12 attention calls) recomputed the O(n²) score matrix, topk, and mask 12 times. Now one model-level `SparseIndexer` computes the selection **once per forward** from the embeddings, and all blocks reuse it. This was the biggest win.

2. **FlexAttention kernel.** The short path's SDPA-with-dense-bias-mask was the profiled bottleneck (forfeits flash attention). Now a compiled FlexAttention kernel applies the indexer bias inside a fused kernel — ~2.3x faster on the attention op itself. SDPA path kept as CPU/small-head fallback.

3. **Detached bias for prelude/coda.** Flex's backward through the bias tensor was 33% of step time. Prelude/coda blocks now get a gradient-detached view of the bias; only the shared block's loops backprop into the indexer. Indexer still trains, backward cost drops.

4. **FP4 quantizer**: `bucketize` instead of an n×8 distance tensor, and detach-trick STE instead of custom autograd.Function.

On your NVFP4 expectation: at 1M params the model is kernel-launch-bound, not matmul-bound — FP4 measured only 3% of step time, and torch 2.10 exposes no actual FP4 tensor-core matmul for this GPU. NVFP4 speedups exist for billion-param models on Blackwell with TransformerEngine; here it's quality-preserving QAT, not a speedup. Physically no path to "skyrocket" from FP4 at this scale — the wins had to come from attention.

Also: STM OOM auto-shrink works (run survived `stm oom: micro batch 256 -> 128` instead of dying), and shrunk batch now persists across epochs/rounds.

**Caveat in the current run:** STM round 3 has NaN-diverged (rounds 1-2 fine). Pre-NaN checkpoints are intact and the tournament will pick among them, but round 3 is wasted. I'll dig into the NaN cause when the run finishes and report final scores.
